headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Khoj indexes personal notes while Opik exposes a REST API and both have broad egress, but no shared channel or direct interaction is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and has optional web search, so prompt-injection via content it ingests is plausible. Opik only exposes a REST API and no shared channel between the pair is documented, so the bridge is indirect rather than default. The pathway exists but appears to require unusual user wiring.
conditions: IF Khoj ingests attacker-controlled notes or web content as trusted instructions
IF Opik is configured to pass its API payloads into Khoj without sanitization
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on retrieved content
Restrict Khoj to trusted note sources only
Add a provenance tag to all Opik-fed content
Require manual review before acting on retrieved instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Opik exposes a REST API with broad network egress. A shared workspace is not documented, but if either side forwards note content or transcripts into the other, sensitive data could leave the local boundary. Uncertainty about the exact integration pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes personal notes that contain sensitive data
IF Opik receives those notes or derived transcripts through its REST API or logs them externally
mitigations: Limit indexed folders to non-sensitive content
Turn off or minimize external logging on Opik
Use separate API keys and principals
Redact transcripts before sending them to Opik
requires-engineering: add field-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj is read-only on the filesystem and does not modify git state; Opik’s profile only shows a REST API and no local write capability. With no overlapping write surface documented, direct resource contention looks limited. The main conflict risk is operational, not destructive.
conditions: IF an orchestrator maps Opik API actions onto the same mutable resource Khoj reads from
IF a shared external service is written by both agents without coordination
mitigations: Keep Khoj read-only on shared data
Avoid routing Opik writes to Khoj-managed files
Serialize any shared-resource updates in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes and documents, and Opik can consume API inputs for evaluation or observability. If Opik treats Khoj output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream reports or actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Khoj-generated text as ground truth
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks Khoj outputs before Opik uses them
mitigations: Add a verification gate before Opik consumes Khoj output
Label Khoj output as untrusted provenance
Sample-check a few outputs before automation
requires-engineering: implement citation-based validation

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, which may include regulated data, while Opik’s profile does not document residency or retention controls. Because the pair lacks documented compliance alignment, any regulated content routed from Khoj into Opik could create a retention or residency mismatch. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF personal notes contain regulated data
IF Opik stores, logs, or processes that data under a different retention or residency policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated notes from Khoj indexing
Review Opik retention settings before use
Document data-class handling for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows
